title: Toward the limits of complexity of interstellar chemistry: Rotational spectroscopy and astronomical search for n- and i-butanal
question: Provide accurate rotational frequencies of n- and i-butanal in the millimeter-wave region, search for them toward Sgr B2(N) and G+0.693-0.027, and test the level of complexity that interstellar chemistry can reach in star-forming regions.

data.sensitivity: 0.35 mJy beam^-1 to 1.1 mJy beam^-1 rms per spectral channel (median 0.8 mJy beam^-1)

what.value: Previously measured microwave lines for n-butanal (7.5-18.5 GHz)

evidence.quote: All in all, we measured more than 2800 rotational transitions for the cis-gauche n-PrCHO along with 1375 transitions for the cis-trans conformer, including in the data set the microwave lines previously observed by Hotopp et al. (2012).

what.value: Previously measured microwave data and dipole moments for i-butanal

evidence.quote: At the first stage of the spectral analysis, we employed predictions based on the spectroscopic parameters from (cite: 1986Stiefvatera), including the experimental values of the electric dipole-moment components.
We note that a set of transitions from the previous microwave data from (cite: 1986Stiefvatera) was also included in the fit with an adequate weight.
We used the spectroscopic predictions of (cite: Smirnov14) for acetaldehyde.

what.value: Spectroscopic predictions for syn and gauche propanal from CDMS catalog (tag 58505 version 2 and tag 58519 version 1)

evidence.quote: We employed the spectroscopic predictions derived for butanal in Sect. 4 and the predictions available in the Cologne Database of Molecular Spectroscopy (CDMS) catalog (cite: Mueller05) for syn and gauche propanal (tag 58505 version 2 and tag 58519 version 1, respectively), which are based on (cite: Zingsheim17).

what.value: LTE results for s-C2H5CHO toward G+0.693-0.027

evidence.quote: We show in Table 6 the molecular ratios of the different aldehydes, using also the LTE results of s-C$_2$H$_5$CHO from (cite: rivilla2020).

what.value: Methanol column density of 2 x 10^19 cm^-2 toward Sgr B2(N1S)

evidence.loc: Discussion: Interstellar chemistry of acetaldehyde, propanal, and butanal
evidence.quote: This value coincides exactly with the observational ratio, using the methanol column density of $2 \times 10^{19}$ cm$^{-2}$ provided by (cite: Motiyenko20) (see their Table 3).

what.value: LTE model of more than 120 species identified toward G+0.693-0.027

evidence.quote: To evaluate if the transitions are blended with emission from other species, we also considered the LTE model that predicts the total contribution of the more than 120 species identified so far toward G+0.693-0.027 (e.g., (cite: requenatorres2008; zeng2018; rivilla2019; rivilla2020; jimenez2020; rodriguez2021a; rodriguez2021b; rivilla2021discovery),b).

recipe.goal: Quantum chemical computations of n- and i-butanal conformers
recipe.method: Geometry optimization and harmonic vibrational frequency calculations at B2PLYP-D3BJ/aug-cc-pVTZ and CCSD/cc-pVTZ levels, followed by single-point CCSD(T)/CBS energy calculations.
key_parameters: n=3 (aug-cc-pVTZ) and n=4 (aug-cc-pVQZ) for CBS extrapolation

recipe.goal: Laboratory measurement and spectroscopic fitting of millimeter-wave rotational spectra of n- and i-butanal
recipe.method: Measure room-temperature absorption spectra from 75 to 325 GHz, assign transitions, fit rotational and centrifugal distortion constants using Watson's A-reduced Hamiltonian in the I^r-representation, and compute rotational and vibrational partition functions.
key_parameters: Gas pressure ~20 ubar, modulation frequency 10.2 kHz, modulation depth 20-35 kHz, 2f demodulation with 30 ms time constant
J up to 150 for Q_r calculation of gauche i-PrCHO; vibrational modes below 1000 cm^-1 for Q_v
assumptions: Experimental uncertainty of unblended symmetric lines is about 30 kHz; harmonic approximation for vibrational partition function

recipe.goal: LTE spectral modeling and upper limit determination toward Sgr B2(N1S) using ALMA ReMoCA data
recipe.method: Extract spectrum toward Sgr B2(N1S), build a population diagram for acetaldehyde across three torsional states to constrain temperature, compute LTE synthetic spectra in Weeds for acetaldehyde and all identified molecules, and derive column density upper limits for propanal and n-/i-butanal.
key_parameters: V_sys = 62 km s^-1, emitting size = 2.0'', T_rot = 250 K and 170 K, linewidth = 5.0 km s^-1, V_off = 0.0 km s^-1
assumptions: LTE assumption justified by high densities; torsional temperature equal to rotational temperature; propanal and butanal trace the same region and physical parameters as acetaldehyde.

recipe.goal: LTE spectral modeling and upper limit determination toward G+0.693-0.027
recipe.method: Implement new spectroscopy into MADCUBA-SLIM, fit unblended transitions of CH3CHO, and determine 3-sigma integrated intensity upper limits for n- and i-butanal conformers using unblended transitions.
key_parameters: For butanal upper limits: T_rot = 12 K, V_LSR = 69 km s^-1, Delta V = 21 km s^-1, Q_v = 1 (neglected)
assumptions: LTE assumption; conformers of n-butanal modeled as independent species without taking into account their zero-point energy due to low excitation temperature.

recipe.goal: Comparison of observational aldehyde abundances and ratios with gas-grain astrochemical models
recipe.method: Compare observed column density ratios and excitation temperatures toward Sgr B2(N1S) and G+0.693-0.027 with the hot-core chemical kinetics model of Garrod et al. (2021) and radical abundance proxies.
key_parameters: Slow warm-up timescale model setup for Sgr B2(N1S); cold grain-surface ratios for G+0.693-0.027
assumptions: Ice radical ratios (C2H5:C3H7 and C3H7:C4H9) serve as proxies for gas-phase or grain-surface production rates of propanal and butanal.

score_reason: The laboratory spectroscopy, partition functions, target coordinates, and LTE model parameters (size, temperature, linewidth, velocity offset, vibrational/conformational correction factors) are thoroughly documented and transition lists are at CDS. However, reproducing the exact astronomical upper limits from scratch requires the custom-reduced ReMoCA spectrum (Melosso et al. 2020), the full background LTE model of all contaminating species in Sgr B2(N1S) and G+0.693-0.027, and the non-ALMA single-dish spectra.
rediscovery_reason: The ALMA project 2016.1.00074.S is public, the spectroscopic catalogs are public at CDS, the exact pixel coordinate for Sgr B2(N1S) and all five Weeds LTE parameters are explicitly tabulated, and the main results are numeric column densities and upper limits.
